A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IDD research work. All 30 pages of v1 and 36 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original synthetic-stream experiments, Gaussian translation experiments, FlowCAP-II detection results and Reddit sentiment analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds runtime measurements, a marginal-density comparison, revised Reddit results and Google Trends correlation analysis.

M1.justification: The reference barycenter, OT displacement representation, MFPCA, T2/SPE statistics and empirical-quantile alarm rule are retained. Splitting the pseudocode into calibration and monitoring algorithms and documenting solver configurations do not establish a substantive change to the detector.

E1.justification: Appendix Q adds Google Trends search-volume data for vaccine-related queries as an external validation proxy. The synthetic shift families, FlowCAP-II task and Reddit domain remain unchanged; the revised Reddit time split belongs primarily to evaluation protocol.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds KDE-Marginal to the copula-shift comparison. The Reddit comparison in Figure 4 adds Hotelling T2 and Scan-B alongside F-CPD and NEWMA. The original principal baselines remain; the C-chart discussed more prominently in v2 was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The Reddit study changes calibration from January 1–February 26 to December 2–January 30, retaining 50 calibration observations, and expands monitoring from 28 to 50 observations starting January 31. v2 also revises event-selection rules, introduces Spearman correlation against an external proxy and adds separate calibration/monitoring timing metrics. This substantially revises one of the two real-world evaluations.

E4.justification: v2 adds a full-distribution versus marginal-monitoring diagnostic in Table 7, computational-cost analysis in Appendix M, and calibration-window sensitivity and external-proxy validation in Appendix Q. These address representation, efficiency and robustness questions beyond the original benchmark results. Appendix K adds calibration-length guidance, but does not report an empirical n0 sweep.

E5.justification: Figure 11 newly reports Spearman correlation p-values and n=48; Appendix Q acknowledges that the correlations are not significant. For example, IDD SPE has rho=0.170 and p=0.249. The existing synthetic practice of means and standard errors over 10 replications is retained, with no documented increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds runtime results, KDE-Marginal scores, AML delay curves and proxy correlations, and replaces Reddit results under the revised split. The regenerated d=50 copula table also changes values: v1 Table 9 reports Log-KDE ARL1=1.0±0.0 at N=50, whereas v2 Table 14 reports 3.2±0.7, with reported ARL0 changing from 102.6 to 100.0. These are revised results, not evidence of a same-setting improvement in IDD.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.12 and new Appendix J extend the theory to sustained post-change Gaussian mean shifts, deriving noncentral statistic distributions and an ARL1 expression, plus bounds without Gaussianity. This is a focused extension; the existing radial-isometry, calibration, spectral-truncation and Gaussian-translation arguments are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: intrinsic distribution-valued monitoring through Wasserstein tangent fields, a two-chart detector, theoretical guarantees and advantages for geometric distributional shifts. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix L newly emphasize settings where simpler detectors match or outperform IDD and explain their sufficient-statistic advantages. Appendix K discusses small-calibration limitations. Appendix Q replaces the earlier strong event-alignment narrative with discussion of unmatched alarms, a data gap, window sensitivity and nonsignificant proxy correlations, although some strong captions and inconsistent interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and extensive implementation disclosures in Appendix N/Table 6: solver calls, regularization, stopping tolerances, barycenter settings, flow architectures, training parameters and the variance-explained truncation rule. These mainly document existing experiments. Reproducibility remains imperfect: solver choices conflict between prose and Table 6, and FlowCAP batch sizes differ across Table 6 and Appendices M and P.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited research and novelty positioning are substantively retained. Changes such as the year listed for Villani’s Topics in Optimal Transportation and edition information are bibliographic updates to the same works.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies notation, separates calibration and monitoring pseudocode, revises case-study explanations, inserts appendix sections and updates publication and acknowledgement text. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact; much of the expansion reflects added scientific content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 3 becomes a two-panel F1/delay display with a clearer legend, Figure 4 is redrawn with six monitoring panels and event annotations, and Figure 11 adds proxy comparisons. New Tables 3–7 display scenario summaries, timings, implementation settings and marginal-monitoring results. Most earlier synthetic figures are retained and relocated rather than newly generated displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through measured costs, a targeted marginal baseline, implementation details and a code link, while more explicitly acknowledging where IDD loses. These address concrete omissions in v1. The net gain is limited by inconsistent reporting: Figure 3 and Appendix P show AML delays around 2–3 while the main text retains approximately 1, and solver and batch-size disclosures disagree across sections. The additions therefore support a modest improvement, not a clear major one.
